claims.text: When the order of classifier aggregation in bagging is random, generalization error typically decreases as the number of classifiers in the ensemble increases.
Devising an appropriate ordering for classifier aggregation causes generalization error to reach a minimum at intermediate numbers of classifiers.
The minimum generalization error achieved through ordered aggregation lies below the asymptotic error of standard bagging.

evidence.description: When this order is random, the generalization error typically decreases as the number of classifiers in the ensemble increases.

methodologies.name: Ordered Aggregation Ensemble Pruning
methodologies.description: Pruning bagging ensembles by modifying the order of classifier aggregation and retaining a fraction of the ordered classifiers.

limitations.text: In the original bagging algorithm, the order of aggregation is left unspecified.
